name: Sun and sand
era_span: The Voyager Era for all seven, with no year number. Kaelis's and Khaeron's cards state it; the other five state no era, and this record sets their shared events in it beside those two. Order: the Lost Prince in the Glass Storms comes before Xhael's ascension rite and the burning of Solfatara; the Red-Dune Severing comes before the Black Oasis, and the Black Oasis before Zahur's refusal to sell the Hidden Oasis, with that pair unfixed against Solfatara's burning; after the burning come Rajhak's relighting of the dead forge and the ash on the Dust Coast, in either order, and last the parley at the magma scar. Everyone here lives one life in one era. WORLD.md flags every Voyager Era card for the check Ignatius's card raises.

members.line: Zahur Vane · The Silt Walker. He is a gatekeeper and wayfinder of the Guides of the Lost Meridian, "a neutral order of wayfinders", and he is called the Weaver of the Blind Road, Keeper of the Sun-Dial Rites and the Soft Trap. His card makes him human, "a nomad lineage of the Great Sand Sea", deep brown of skin and coiled of hair, and hard to kill with heat or thirst. He leads seekers toward lost Wellsprings and judges, without telling them, whether they deserve to arrive. His order is the closest thing he has to a home, and he answers to its purpose. The Great Sand Sea is the nearest thing he has to kin. He kept guarding the Hidden Oasis of the Great Sand Sea when he could have sold its location, and he pays for every working in his own body's water. He can turn the ground under a charging man to slurry and let it close around him like stone when he stops. He leaves no print unless he chooses to. Gold at his ears, the Sun-Dials, carries the tremor of the earth to him and hums near an active Wellspring or a disturbance of the void. His card keeps two incidents. He walked a band of ambushing bandits into a soft patch of the desert, and nobody saw them again. He guided a young royal through the Glass Storms to find a cure for his father, and took his pay in a story nobody had heard. He explains nothing. "The sand does not need to be hard to kill you. It only needs to be deep. Step carefully."

Raelen Vor'Skai · The Gilded Scourge. He is called the White-Jackal, the Sand-Vein Seraph and Gold-Eater, and his epithet is He Who Bleeds in Silence: an independent inscription-bearer, glyph-bound and desert-blooded. No Order holds him. Several track him for what the mark on his hand might be worth, some fearing it and some wanting it, and he answers to no charter and works alone across the southern Realms. The mark is an incomplete sigil bound into his palm, the Sable Contract, which ties him to a Wellspring he tried to reject; neither he nor the ritual that tried could unmake it. That ritual was the Red-Dune Severing. It half-succeeded at cutting the mark out of him, his Crystal broke and opened inside it hours apart, and he came out "seeing in two lights instead of one." The half that was cut away is missing, and his whole road points toward finding it. At the Black Oasis he stopped a Wellspring inversion at the cost of a chunk of his own memory, and nobody there knows his name for it. He wears gold rings and burns them in his Rite, and each ring burned is gone for good. He tells what the mark means only as far as a diagnosis needs. His card leaves open whether the missing half still answers when he calls the Rite, "from wherever it ended up."

Kaelis Aranthor · The Sunbound Blade. He is a desert-born freeblade and momentum duelist of the Voyager Era, called the Crimson Horizon and Oathbreaker of No Banner, once a freeblade mercenary and now an independent power who owes no banner and answers to no house. Several factions would sooner keep him as a wildcard than meet him as an enemy. He has fought for most of them. Whoever hired him last is a transaction, by his own design. The exception is anyone he has chosen to protect. His card's Catalyst was a contract that put him on the losing side of a fight he could have walked away from. He stayed, and the coin stopped mattering partway through. Since then employers negotiate with him. Every clean movement he makes feeds the next. He can spend all of it in one burst and start again from nothing. A forced stop in the middle of a run can turn the stored force inward, and his crimson scarf is there for that. He explains himself freely, mostly for the pleasure of watching people learn too late that the explanation was accurate. "You mistake confidence for arrogance. I simply know which way this is going."

Xhael Ten'Kor · The Ember Regent. He is the exiled sun-prince of the former Temple-State of Solfatara, a dominion arbiter and "Walking Conflux of Molten Essence", and now a wandering sovereign in self-imposed exile whom the Guild Accord registers as a Realm-Hazard. An Exuroth Wellspring beneath Solfatara's palace vaults raised him. He seized divine power through an incomplete ascension rite. The rite burned the throne to ash and crowned him in molten gold, and forty thousand people died. His card reads every other tie against that debt. He is bound to the magma scar over Solfatara, which he did not make on purpose and cannot fully disown. The Obsidian Crown is fused to his skull. It vents what his body cannot hold. He draws the heat around him into himself, and he can raise the air about him to burning light. A long fight risks a detonation over a wide radius, and his human form holds only for a span his card sets. He has brought Varūn caravans through volcanic storms, unprompted. Accord envoys have engaged him once, without casualties. A monarch does not narrate his own workings, and he does not. His epigraph names him a man who mistook light for salvation.

Rajhak Tarun · The Ember-Blooded. He is a flame-walker, a Wellspring interpreter, and a freelance arcanist who serves the Guild Accord as Wellspring Liaison without a Division seat. His card makes him frontierfolk and Verdant, of the border tribes of the Scorched Plains, ground thought lifeless until his people learned to coax Essence out of ash; it marks that lineage unattested. He goes between nomadic clans and Guild envoys and speaks for unregistered Cores and fire-touched communities beyond Concord jurisdiction, and neither side owns him. The Research and Archives Division values his grasp of thermic Essence law. Enforcement tolerates him for results. Taverns call him prophet and pyromancer and have not decided which. He relit a dead Concord forge by spilling his own blood on its altar, in front of witnesses, and the forge is the seed his card names. Nearby Essence keeps his heartbeat, and volatile ground steadies near him. When he opens a vein the blood ignites, and the signs he traces in the smoke bind heat, truth and feeling into law until a wind unwrites them. Each rite needs its interval before the next, and he is restless in it. His twin oath rings sound near broken vows. He speaks in parables and will not say how anything works. "Every spark wants to grow. I just remind it how." His card leaves open whether the Ember-Blooded are a bloodline or a discipline his people taught the blood.

Khaeron Vant · The Ember Host. He is called the Bladeshrine of Cinerion and the Mask-Bound, and his epithet is He Who Makes Oaths Burn: an Abythron-touched executioner and ash-fire ritualist of the Voyager Era. He is a free Therosian executioner, formally bound to a minor Abythron cult that holds him more in custody than in loyalty, and he drifts between Cinerion-aligned cults and Accord warbands. Cinerion-aligned Accord warpriests court him to license his execution work. A horned mask-spirit is anchored in his spine. He looked at his own record and accepted himself as the mask's vessel, and since then the mask argues with him and does not own him. Burning blades hang at his flanks from a lattice of his own vertebrae. He drives four knives into ground, corpses or walls and raises a chamber in which every lie, hesitation or broken oath blooms as ash-fire in the offender's lungs. Each casting shaves away a sliver of the memories he had before the Pact. Those his brands kill leave dim echoes he can burn for strength, and burning them erases them further from the record. A strong Verdantia or Benediction current makes his brands sputter. "I am the altar and the knife. You only choose how much of you burns." He explains the altar he considers himself to be, and he explains it often.

Rafik Al'Seren · The Sapphire Mirage. He is a dreamcaster, a Wellspring cartographer and a freelance informant, a Wellspring Interpreter and wanderer "currently based out of the Veyran Free Ports." The Guild Accord classes him a civic-observation operative, non-hostile and under watch, and occasionally useful to its archivists. He was born near the Mirithane Wellspring during a sandstorm bloom. A failed Sublimatio ritual scarred his left eye, and since then he sees heat currents and soul-light whether he wants to or not. He has brought pilgrims and caravans of the Varūn border communities through Aether storms, unofficially and without asking thanks. He also sells Wellspring coordinates to whoever pays. His chart, the Scroll of Sublimare, glows when a new node wakes, and it is his warning and his income. He can hide a small party in bent light and sound, send his sight along a thread to far places, and raise copies of himself that carry part of his real mass, so that every blow they take lands on him. Long exposure bleeds his memory. He will translate his own tricks for the right audience or the right price. "Truth is a mirage that survives only until someone believes in it."

events.name: The Lost Prince in the Glass Storms
events.when: The Voyager Era, before Xhael's ascension rite and the burning of Solfatara, while he was a young prince and Kaelis still took freeblade contracts. The crossing is Zahur's card's incident "The Lost Prince"; that the young royal was Xhael, and that Kaelis rode with him, is new.
events.where: The Glass Storms of the Great Sand Sea (Zahur's card). No page places the Great Sand Sea; this record sets it in the dry south of the Outer World (WORLD §3, §5), where Raelen's card puts the southern Realms.
events.what: Xhael Ten'Kor came out of Solfatara as a young prince to find a cure for his father, and the road to it ran through the Glass Storms. The Temple-State hired Kaelis Aranthor to keep him alive on that road. At the edge of the sand the Guides of the Lost Meridian gave the prince Zahur Vane. Zahur walked the party in by the gold at his ears, halting them wherever it told him the ground was soft. When the first storm rose, Kaelis wanted to cross before it closed, and Zahur put the party in the lee of a dune and made them sit. In that storm the prince was lost from the lee. Kaelis did not find him. Zahur heard his footfalls through the gold, walked out into the storm, and brought him back. After that the party moved when Zahur moved. The prince found what he had crossed for and carried it back out through the storms. At the end of the road Zahur named his price, a story nobody had heard, and the prince told it to him alone. Kaelis took the Temple-State's coin. What each took: Zahur took the story, and he has never told it. Xhael took the thing he had crossed for, and the one story of his that the Great Sand Sea keeps. Kaelis took his fee, for a charge he had lost in the storm and another man had found.

events.name: The Red-Dune Severing
events.when: The Voyager Era, before the Black Oasis; its place against Solfatara's burning is not fixed. It is Raelen's card's Catalyst. That Khaeron held the knife, and that Raelen came to him for it, is new.
events.where: The red dunes that give the Severing its name (Raelen's card), in the southern Realms of the Outer World (WORLD §3). No page places them.
events.what: Raelen wanted the mark out of his hand. He looked for a knife that would cut a binding, and he found Khaeron Vant among the Cinerion-aligned cults. Khaeron took the work, and Raelen paid him in gold. On the red dunes Khaeron cut into Raelen's palm with the Ash-Gorge blades, and the blood from the cut went grey and drifted off as ash. Half the mark came away. The other half held in the palm, bound past anything the knife could part. Inside the same rite, hours apart, Raelen's Crystal broke and then opened, and he came out of it seeing in two lights instead of one. When the rite broke off, the cut half lay on neither the sand nor the blades. Neither man has it. Word of the Severing reached the minor Abythron cult that holds Khaeron's formal allegiance, and from then on it has been one of the Orders tracking Raelen. What each took: Raelen took the half of the mark still bound in his palm, the loss of the half that was cut, two lights to see by, and a cult on his trail. Khaeron took his fee, a cut he could not finish, and his cult's interest in the man he had cut.

events.name: The Black Oasis
events.when: The Voyager Era, after the Red-Dune Severing and before Zahur's card's Catalyst. The inversion and Raelen's stopping of it are his card's; the chart, the buyers and Zahur's part are new.
events.where: The Black Oasis (Raelen's card), which this record sets at the edge of the Great Sand Sea, within reach of Zahur's gold. No page places it.
events.what: The Wellspring under the oasis was on Rafik Al'Seren's chart, and he sold its coordinates to buyers who paid. The buyers came by the chart, with no guide, and set to work at the well-head. The Wellspring began to invert. Out in the sand, the gold at Zahur's ears hummed with it, and he came. He led the people of the oasis out a few at a time, along ground that would hold them, and did not tell them why he had come. Raelen came in off the sand while they were leaving. He went down to the well-head alone and stopped the inversion, and a chunk of his own memory went with it. The people saw a stranger go down to the water and come back up. None of them learned his name. Zahur saw what the stranger had done. He has told no one. What each took: Raelen took a gap in his memory and a place where nobody knows his name for what he did. Zahur took the people he led out, and the sight of what a sold Wellspring becomes. When a price was offered him afterward for the location of the Hidden Oasis, he refused it, and that refusal is his card's Catalyst. Rafik took the price of the coordinates, paid before the buyers set out, and the Black Oasis stays on his chart as what is left of it.

events.name: Ash on the Dust Coast
events.when: The Voyager Era, after the burning of Solfatara, in Xhael's exile. Xhael's and Rafik's cards each say they aided Varūn caravans through storms; this crossing, and Kaelis's part in it, are new.
events.where: The Aurelian Dust Coast, the mineral desert between the Drakhal Spine and the sea (WORLD §5; `The Outer World · The Southern Pan.md`), on a caravan road under ash blown west off the Spine's volcanic belt.
events.what: A Varūn caravan was on the Dust Coast road, bound back west with copper and nitre. Kaelis Aranthor rode with it as its hired blade. Rafik Al'Seren walked with it on nobody's commission. A volcano on the Spine went up, and the Varūn drovers called it a Prometheic Surge, as their volcanologists do. The ash came down the wind over the coast with an Aether storm inside it. The caravan stopped. Kaelis stood still in the ash with the rest of it. Rafik read the heat currents through the ash with his scarred eye and found where the ground was cool enough to walk. Then a light came out of the ash ahead of them. Xhael Ten'Kor walked down the line of beasts and drew the heat around the caravan into himself. He went at its head. The caravan followed his light through the storm into clear air. He left them at the edge of the ash before his form's limit came, and he asked for nothing. Kaelis knew him for the prince he had been hired to keep alive in the Glass Storms. Xhael gave no sign that he knew Kaelis. What each took: Xhael took nothing, and the drovers carried word of him west. Rafik took a road through the ash and a close sight of the Ember Regent at work. He carried what he had seen to the Guild Accord's archivists, and it is the word that brought the envoys to the scar. Kaelis took his fee, a caravan brought through whole, and a second sight of the prince.

events.name: The parley at the magma scar
events.when: The Voyager Era, after Ash on the Dust Coast, and after Rajhak relit the dead Concord forge, which is his card's Catalyst. It is the one engagement Xhael's card records. Who went, how it ran and where the forge stood are new.
events.where: The magma scar over Solfatara (Xhael's card), and the Concord forge on the road below it. No page places Solfatara; this record sets it in the Outer World (WORLD §3).
events.what: The Concord forge on the road below Solfatara went dead the year the Temple-State burned. Rajhak Tarun relit it by spilling his own blood on its altar, with Accord witnesses standing by. When Rafik's word of the Ember Regent reached the archivists, the Accord sent envoys up to the scar to engage him, and they took Rajhak as their liaison. The Cinerion-aligned warpriests of an Accord warband went with them and brought Khaeron Vant, to show the envoys what a licensed executioner could do. The Flux over the scar was high. Where Rajhak stood, the ground kept his heartbeat and steadied. Xhael came down to meet them. Khaeron drove four knives into the crust around the meeting and raised his Shrine, so that any lie told inside it would bloom as ash-fire in the liar's lungs. Rajhak's oath rings sounded the whole time he stood near the executioner. The envoys asked Xhael what had happened at Solfatara, and he told them what had happened and nothing of how. Nothing burned. The envoys went back down with no one hurt, and the Accord entered him in its register as a Realm-Hazard. What each took: Xhael took an entry in the Accord's register, and the knowledge that the Accord can find him at the scar. Rajhak took a result, which is what Enforcement tolerates him for, and the Research and Archives Division's regard for his grasp of thermic law. His rings have sounded near Khaeron Vant whenever the two have met since. Khaeron took the loss of a sliver of memory from before the Pact, spent on a chamber where nothing burned, in front of the warpriests who had brought him there to show what he could do.

ties.summary: He walked the young prince through the Glass Storms, brought him back when the storm took him from the party, and took his pay in a story only Zahur has heard.
They brought the prince through the Glass Storms together: the guide who sat the storm out, and the blade who wanted to outrun it and lost his charge in it.
Solfatara hired Kaelis to keep its prince alive in the Glass Storms; later, in the ash on the Dust Coast, the exiled prince walked out the caravan Kaelis was guarding and gave no sign he knew him.
Zahur led the people out of the Black Oasis while Raelen went down to the inverting Wellspring; he saw what the stranger did and has told no one.
Rafik sold the Black Oasis's coordinates and the buyers came by his chart with no guide; Zahur led the oasis-folk out, and later refused any price for the Hidden Oasis.
Raelen paid a chunk of his memory to stop the inversion that followed the sale of Rafik's coordinates; nobody has told him whose chart it was.
They brought a Varūn caravan through the ash on the Dust Coast together; Rafik carried what he saw of the Ember Regent to the Accord's archivists, and the envoys came.
Kaelis guarded the Varūn caravan in the ash on the Dust Coast, and Rafik found its road through.
Rajhak relit the Concord forge that went dead when Solfatara burned, and stood as the Accord's liaison at the parley on the scar, where the ground kept his heartbeat.
Khaeron raised his Shrine around the parley at the scar; Xhael answered the envoys inside it, and nothing burned.

They stood in one chamber at the scar for different masters in the Accord, the envoys' liaison and the warpriests' executioner, and Rajhak's oath rings sounded the whole time; Rajhak carries the Verdantia current Khaeron's card names as his counter.
Raelen hired Khaeron to cut the mark from his palm at the Red-Dune Severing; half came away, the half that came away is lost to both, and Khaeron's cult has tracked Raelen since.

outward.wants: The buyer, or a buyer's agent, who offered a price for the Hidden Oasis's location and was refused on the day his card names as his Catalyst. His card names no one; an officer of an Accord Division or a house that wants the Wellspring would fit.
An officer of one of the Orders that track him and want the mark, which his card leaves unnamed. This record makes Khaeron's minor Abythron cult one of them; the Weaver may give him another.
The person he chose to protect in the losing fight of his Catalyst. His card leaves that person unnamed.
A survivor of Solfatara. It should be someone who knew the court before the rite, lived through it, and holds him to the debt of the forty thousand.
An archivist of the Research and Archives Division, the one who reads his reports.
A Cinerion-aligned Accord warpriest. It should be the one who brought him to the scar to show the envoys what licensed execution could do, and who still wants his work licensed.
His handler: the Guild Accord officer who holds his civic-observation file.

card_contradictions: Realm-Hazard, card against wiki. Xhael's card: "registered by the Guild Accord as a Tier 6 Realm-Hazard." The Bestiary sets Realm Hazard a tier higher: "T7, Realm Hazard" (`wiki/The Bestiary/Aberrations.md`, and the tier table in `wiki/The Bestiary/The Bestiary.md`). `The Guild Accord.md` runs its Threat Tiers from T1 to T9 and names no Realm-Hazard register. This record names no tier.

Oblivara, two cards against the Limina page. Khaeron's card: "the current actually erasing a victim's Echo when a brand takes hold". Raelen's card: "Sable Pulse's emotional erasure is Oblivara's, not Dissolution's." `Limina · Entropy, Void and Mind.md`: "the practitioner's identity is redundantly encoded against erasure", with the stat effect "Resistance to conceptual erasure and perceptual manipulation." The cards make Oblivara the eraser, and the page makes it the guard against erasure.

Veyran. Rafik's card: "currently based out of the Veyran Free Ports." The Southern Pan page: "The Kingdom of Veyran, a horse-and-grain monarchy, exists by treaty guarantee because the empire values what it grows.", set in the Southern Grass Sea, and WORLD.md §3 lists Veyran among the Outer World's polities. Ravenn Kaelor's card gives "Kingdom of Veyran descent". Aeldoris Vanthryx's card: "Veyran is unattested; see the migration note." No page names the Free Ports.

Therosian. Khaeron's card: "Free Therosian executioner". The Southern Pan page names a kingdom of the Five Rivers: "Therosan, river-and-fortress state specialising in engineering, masonry and Aether-efficient warding." `The Abyssal Depths · Prometheus, Zar'thuun, Vohrin.md` calls Prometheus "The Flame of Theros" and says "the Scorched Realms of Theros became the foundation of post-war rebirth". Valen Therosian carries the word as a surname. No card or page says which Khaeron's word means, and this record places nothing by it.

The Voyager Era. Kaelis's and Khaeron's cards: "Voyager Era". WORLD.md §1: "The other Voyager cards need the same check.", the check Ignatius's card raises by saying Voyager Era while the Sanctum Lux page writes Darius alive. This record sets the cluster in the Voyager Era on those two cards' word and leaves the check open.
